evidence.reason: The lexer only carries triple-quote state. When `findClose` returns -1 for a single/double-quoted short string, line 390 blanks through end-of-line but leaves `state` as null. On the next physical line of a Python backslash-continued short string, the literal's actual closing quote is therefore treated as a new opening quote, blanking text such as `; pytest.skip(` and causing the added marker to be missed. This is a false negative in the existing Python skip-marker detection, not an expansion or a proposal; the contract's accepted docstring-prose cost concerns triple-quote state, not this short-string state bug.
